narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Dry until evening showers, with thunder possible from midday, peaking this evening. 30°C (86°F) high, 19°C (66°F) low. Sky mostly clear early as reported, mostly cloudy at midday and overcast in the evening. Wind NNE early and SSW at midday; gusts to 35 km/h (19 kt). UV index 8.7 (very high). Air quality 43 (good) at Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central, the highest of 3 stations. As of 06:01, reports through 04:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 21°C (70°F); low so far 19°C (66°F); peak sustained 4 km/h (2 kt); sky mostly clear.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Friday, with rain possible from Thursday and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies partly cloudy Wednesday, then mostly cloudy Thursday and Friday. Friday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs 29 to 31°C (84 to 88°F). At this lead Best Match has the best record, right 83% of the time over 80 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Tuesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Saturday and Sunday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Monday and Tuesday. Saturday: two of four models wet, highs 27 to 30°C (80 to 86°F). Sunday: three of four models wet, highs around 30°C (86°F). Monday: two of three models wet, highs around 29°C (84°F), thunder possible rather than likely.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Sunday. ECMWF is the wetter solution from Saturday to Sunday; GFS, ICON and UKMO keep it drier. Tuesday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 30°C (85°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 83% of the time over 76 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Convective instability in the hours ahead: UKMO 4590 J/kg, ICON 1990 J/kg, ECMWF 1420 J/kg and GFS 540 J/kg. Thunder likely; any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above the 35 km/h (19 kt) forecast.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Peak gust 28 km/h (15 kt). Any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above this figure; the water is unsafe while one is nearby.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1006 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1014 hPa) — an 8 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is falling. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1012.9 and 1015.1 hPa, falling by 1.6 hPa over three days. Pressure here over the last 24 hours: +0.5 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

On rain the record ranks Best Match first at Day+3, right 83% of the last 30 checks and ECMWF first at Day+7, right 83% of the last 30 checks. On today's high ICON is the warmest model at 30.1°C (86.2°F) and ECMWF the coolest at 29.1°C (84.4°F); the call's 29.8°C (85.6°F) sits between them. Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls a high of 29.0°C (84.2°F) and a dry day, against the call on rain. At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet. At Day+7, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and GFS the weakest. At Day+0, Best Match slightly under-forecasts daytime highs here.

Figures issued 06:01. Written by code; a discussion follows when a model answers.
